Map marker is her Fi photo via /avatar.jpg, falling back to the K initial through the existing data-optional listener.
map.js and map_live.js stopped keeping duplicate copies of the tile layer and markers; map_base.js owns both.

Steps/Rest hero broke a 5-fact middot paragraph into 4 short lines; outdoor_distance() labels distance as outdoors and gives a zero words; explanatory notes added for steps-vs-distance and sleep-vs-naps.
LED control built against the robot session's new POST/GET /led: gateway client methods, two routes, six swatches + on/off on the Robot tab, led.js following the draw-from-the-answer rule.

WebSocket drive transport phone->server: /robot/ws/drive with an explicit cookie check, a server-side pump at 200ms, a 600ms hold expiry, newest-wins takeover, and a full HTTP fallback. Confirmed working end-to-end in Chromium (Link: socket).
Chart drag-scrubbing on all three charts via cloned server-rendered readings (_readings.html macros), never rebuilt in JS.
THE SECOND JOYSTICK: pan/tilt look stick in drive mode. Chris had asked twice and it had never been built -- /robot/look existed with no UI at all.
docs/robot-measurements.md: the three hardware measurements written as steps, plus the look stick's two sign checks.
PR #52 opened; CI green on ubuntu AND windows.
/security-review on the full branch: no findings at confidence >= 8.
discovered: The slow leg for driving is phone->PC (~700ms over Tailscale/LTE), NOT PC->Pi (~1ms wired). So the gateway's own /ws/drive optimises the wrong hop and stays unused. This corrected my own earlier plan.
uvicorn[standard] already brings websockets 17.1, so the WebSocket needed no new dependency.

FastAPI's @app.middleware('http') does NOT run for WebSocket handshakes. Without an explicit cookie check the WS route would have been the only unauthenticated route in the app -- and the one that moves a robot.
SameSite=Lax is what actually blocks cross-site WebSocket hijacking here: a WS handshake is not a top-level navigation, so the cookie is not sent cross-site.
EVERY map screenshot this project has ever taken was the 'Map unavailable' state, because the capture script never stubbed tile requests and tile hosts are unreachable from a sandbox.
The audit server had no photo and ran KONA_MAP_TILES=osm, so the avatar path and the whole Stadia path were never rendered -- which is how a bug existing only under stadia reached Chris's phone.
The robot's front LEDs are on I2C 0x77, not the motor bus, so /led answers while /health says turbopi:false. 'Lights on, will not move' is now a readable diagnostic state.
TURBOPI_MAX_DUTY=55 was a judgement call with no measurement behind it, and the failure to fear is the Pi browning out as the pack sags, not the motors.
There is no mjpg-streamer on the robot: the stream is Python inside TurboPi.py, capped at 20fps by a hardcoded sleep, downscaled with INTER_NEAREST.
decisions: The WebSocket is strictly an optimisation and degrades silently to the POST path; nothing about stopping is load-bearing on it. stopNow stays on HTTP because a stop must be watched landing.
The server-side pump expires after 600ms of silence and sends one stop. Repeating forever would defeat a watchdog that only fires when commands stop arriving.
A stop goes down the socket AND over HTTP, always. The socket arrives first; the POST is the one that can be confirmed.
The look stick is deliberately NOT a dead-man control: a servo holds where it is put, and a camera that recentred on release would be useless for looking around a room.
The look stick is disabled alongside the drive controls (unlike the LEDs) because /look goes through the same RPC server that owns the motors.
Rotation stays on two buttons rather than moving to the right stick: on a holonomic robot the left stick's X is a genuine strafe, so there is no spare axis.
Distance is only shown when labelled 'outdoors' and accompanied by the explanatory sentence -- the two conditions docs/device-capabilities.md set and we had been violating.
Chart readings are rendered server-side and cloned by JS, never rebuilt, so the two renderings cannot drift.
lessons: An inline style= attribute is dropped silently under style-src 'self' with no 'unsafe-inline' -- same trap as inline script. Third time this project has been bitten by a silently-failing CSP rule; there is now a test over the whole template directory.

response.json() REJECTS on a non-JSON body, and a failing server is exactly when the body stops being JSON. Unguarded, that rejection becomes the user-facing message (a screenshot read: Unexpected token 'I', "Internal S"... is not valid JSON).
set.discard() always returns None -- a guard written as `if s.discard(x) is None` never fires. Caught by writing the test to count outcomes rather than inspect the flag.

A fixture that misses something does not fail; it renders the empty state and puts it in front of a reviewer as though it were normal. Same trap as sonar_cm before it, now hit twice more (no photo, osm tiles).
Writing an accurate test stub found a real bug: a node-moving loop terminated only because appendChild reparents. A stub that merely copied would have passed here and hung in Safari.
Keying a set on id() is unsafe when objects can be collected: a reused id would silently suppress a real stop. Use the objects.
open_questions: Will iOS Safari open a ws: connection under connect-src 'self'? No test here can answer it. Drive mode's strip reads Link: socket or Link: polling so Chris can tell at a glance; the fallback is already built either way.
Are the strafe axes correct? Still unmeasured. Stand test written up.
Is tilt's sign correct? Screen-up maps to tilt-up in our code but has never been checked on hardware.
Can TURBOPI_MAX_DUTY rise above 55? Needs the battery-sag measurement on a full pack.
Is the robot camera actually the problem, or is it the 700ms round trip? One drive on home Wi-Fi settles it.
intent: Chris went to bed and gave autonomy for the night. Everything he approved is built, tested on both CI platforms, security-reviewed and pushed as PR #52. The remaining work is all hardware verification that needs him in the room with the robot.
next_task: Chris reviews PR #52 and merges; then runs docs/robot-measurements.md with the robot on a box.
dont_retry: Do not put the WebSocket on the PC->Pi leg -- that hop is ~1ms wired and the gateway's /ws/drive would optimise nothing.
Do not use style= attributes in templates; the CSP drops them silently.
Do not raise the robot camera's resolution before measuring on home Wi-Fi -- the 20fps ceiling is a hardcoded sleep, so 720p can only cost frame rate.
Do not rely on the gate middleware for WebSocket routes; it does not run for handshakes.
